chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:
The Imam is the inheritor of the one who has no inheritor for him.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, referring to the divinely appointed leader

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate of a person with no other relatives according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Imam as the ultimate heir (warith) for those lacking living relatives, a principle central to Shia inheritance jurisprudence (fara'id). It underscores the Imam's dual role as both spiritual guide and temporal authority, ensuring that the deceased's wealth is preserved and distributed according to divine law rather than reverting to the state or treasury. This concept reinforces the continuity of divine authority in managing communal assets during the era of the Imams.
